sections.h2: Where do you take a deed in Marquette County?
sections.html:
Deeds go to the Register of Deeds at 234 W. Baraga Avenue, Marquette, MI 49855, and the counter phone is (906) 225-8415. The county posts weekday hours of 8 to 5. Documents sent through an e-recording vendor can be submitted around the clock, though staff work them between 8 and 4.

The county site explains why timing matters. Michigan uses a race-notice system, so a buyer who records first stands ahead of anyone who shows up later with a competing claim. The office stamps documents in the exact order they are presented, which is why title agents tend to record the same day the lender wires funds.

A house sale in the county usually involves three desks that share the Baraga Avenue courthouse address:

  • The Register of Deeds, for the deed itself, mortgage releases and copies
  • The County Treasurer, at (906) 225-8425, for tax history and delinquent real property bills
  • Equalization and Tax Roll, at (906) 225-8405, for ownership records and parcel maps

sections.h2: What kind of county is Marquette for someone selling a home?
sections.html:
Marquette County is big and thinly settled. It holds 1,808 square miles of land, the most of any Michigan county, with Lake Superior along its north edge and the Huron Mountains inside it. About 47 percent of its 3,425 total square miles is water. The three cities are Marquette, Ishpeming and Negaunee, and Northern Michigan University, founded in 1899, sits in the county seat.

The Census Bureau counted 66,017 residents in April 2020 and estimated 68,064 by July 2025, which makes this the most populous county in the Upper Peninsula. Federal survey figures for 2020 through 2024 show owners valuing a typical house at $216,500, with 69.6 percent of homes lived in by their owners. Typical gross rent was $949 a month, and a typical household earned $65,429.

The Marquette Iron Range, the Cliffs Shaft Mine and the Jackson Mine are among the ten state historical markers in the county. Parcels near the range towns can have long chains of ownership, so ask your title company how far back it will search.

sections.h2: What does a deed filing cost at the Marquette County courthouse annex?
sections.html:
The county charges a flat $30.00 for a deed, however many pages it runs. That amount already folds in the state remonumentation charge and the register's automation charge, so nothing else is tacked on at the window for the recording itself.

Marquette County Register of Deeds price list, as printed on the county's own fee page
What you are buyingPrice
Recording a deed, mortgage or lis pendens$30.00
One document releasing several instruments, per extra instrument$3.00
Treasurer's tax certification, when the deed needs it$5.00
Certifying a recorded document$5.00
Copy of any record, each page$1.00
Copy of a plat, each page$2.00
Name search by the office, per year covered$0.50, with a $5.00 floor

Transfer tax comes on top whenever the deed is taxable. The counter takes cash, check or card, and card use adds a processing charge.

sections.h2: Which part of a Marquette County sale price goes to transfer tax?
sections.html:
Michigan puts the tax on the grantor, the person signing the property over. The county's transfer tax page also says the full consideration has to appear on the deed. A sale price left off the face of the deed can be covered by a valuation affidavit, which the office files at no charge as long as the deed says one is on file.

The state's share is $3.75 on every $500 slice of the price, rounded up for any leftover amount. A $200,000 house has 400 slices, so the state share is $1,500 before the county's share is added. Phone the office for the county's per-slice figure so your net sheet is accurate.

MCL 207.526 carves out several deeds, and the grantor has to say so on the deed. Sellers most often rely on these:

  • Consideration below $100
  • A gift deed to a son, daughter, grandson or granddaughter
  • Transfers following foreclosure, or a deed given to avoid it
  • A land contract that has not yet delivered legal title
  • A corrective quitclaim that only repairs a title flaw

sections.h2: Why would the Marquette County Register of Deeds send a deed back?
sections.html:
The most common reason is paperwork that falls short of MCL 565.201. The office will not draft a deed or advise on one, and it records only originals, so a fax or a plain photocopy goes straight back. A court order must arrive certified by the court, since a "true copy" is refused.

Specific defects that trigger a rejection include:

  • Signer names printed under the signatures that disagree with the notary block
  • No mailing address for the buyer, or no name and address for whoever prepared the deed
  • Ink that is not black or dark blue, or type under 10 point
  • Less than 2 1/2 inches of clear space at the top of page one
  • An opening line that names more than one recordable event
  • Full Social Security numbers left on the page

Anything that is not in English needs an English translation attached.

sections.h2: What does the Marquette County Treasurer check before a deed is accepted?
sections.html:
On a warranty deed or a land contract, the register needs proof from the treasurer that the parcel's taxes are paid for the five years ahead of the deed date. That rule is in MCL 211.135, and it does not reach a plain quitclaim. The treasurer's office is in the Courthouse Annex at the same Baraga Avenue address and keeps weekday hours of 8 to 5.

Each March 1, townships and cities hand the county treasurer whatever real property tax is still open, and the county takes over collection. Delinquent bills can be paid there by debit or credit card. A seller who is behind can clear the account before requesting the certificate, or ask the title company to pay it out of proceeds at the closing table.

The county treasurer also sells county plat books and provides tax histories, which is useful when a buyer wants to see what the parcel has been billed in past years.

sections.h2: How can I search or file Marquette County records without driving to Baraga Avenue?
sections.html:
The online index and images cover deeds from January 1, 1980, and mortgages and miscellaneous documents from January 1, 1983. Older books are open only in person. Copies of pre-1983 records carry a $7.50 tract charge in addition to the per-page price, per the county FAQ.

E-recording is open through four vendors named on the county's page: CSC, ePN, Indecomm Global Services and Simplifile. The county warns that some document types cannot be filed this way, so title companies confirm with the vendor first. If the register rejects an e-filed deed, the notice comes back through the vendor.

The office also warns residents about outside firms that charge $50 or more for a certified deed copy. The county itself sells copies for as little as $1 a page, and owners can enroll in its free Property Fraud Alert service.

sections.h2: What happens to the Marquette County tax bill after the sale closes?
sections.html:
The deed recorded in Marquette triggers a reassessment of the taxable value. Under MCL 211.27a the buyer must report the transfer to the local assessor within 45 days, and the taxable value resets to the state equalized value starting the following year. The register also sends the assessing officers a list of recorded transfers at least monthly.

Marquette County's Equalization office reviews 22 local assessing districts and recommends equalized values to the Board of Commissioners. It also keeps ownership maps, and its page says staff alert owners when a faulty deed has been recorded and suggest a fix. A buyer who wants a parcel list or tax roll extract can buy one: the printed assessment roll runs $0.15 a page with a $35 minimum.

Ask the equalization office at (906) 225-8405 for a tax code number or a parcel map before a closing, and ask your local unit for the bill estimate for the next cycle.

faqs.q: What is the recording fee at the Marquette County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: The flat charge is $30.00 per document. It includes the state survey and automation portions, so no further recording surcharge appears at the counter. Extra instruments released in one document are $3.00 each.

faqs.q: Which party owes transfer tax on a Marquette County house sale?
faqs.a: The seller, meaning the grantor on the deed. The state share is $3.75 per $500 slice of price, and the county adds its own charge. An exempt deed, such as a gift to a child, must state the exemption on its face.

faqs.q: Will Marquette County record a photocopy of my signed deed?
faqs.a: No. Only documents with original signatures are accepted, and court orders must be certified by the court. Call (906) 225-8415 before mailing so the office can confirm the paperwork is complete.

faqs.q: Do I need a tax certificate to sell my Marquette County home?
faqs.a: Yes, for a warranty deed or land contract. The treasurer must show the five prior years of taxes are paid, and the register's fee sheet lists $5.00 for that certification. A quitclaim deed without warranty is excused.

faqs.q: How far back do Marquette County online land records reach?
faqs.a: Deed images and the index start January 1, 1980, and mortgages and miscellaneous papers start January 1, 1983. Anything older is available at the office on Baraga Avenue.
